sentences.text: The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Electronic city Sub-division has foisted charge sheet against this accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage between the accused and deceased Malini was performed on 07.10.2011 at S.M. Marriage Hall, situated at Yelachenahally, Bengaluru.
After marriage both accused and deceased started their marital life along with her family members.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased was blessed with a male child ie CW8 by name Master Charan Kumar.
After sometime, the accused has started to reside separately along with the deceased and their son in separate house at Yelachenahally.

Thereafter, the accused has started to harass the deceased physically and mentally by addicting to bad habit like drinking alcohol and without going for driving work by demanding to bring dowry by way of cash to fulfill his needs.
When the same has been brought to the notice of her parents, the parents of the deceased advised the accused and also paid Rs.5,000/- and Rs.10,000/- sometime on the demand of accused.
About one and a half years back to the date of the incident, the accused along with the deceased and their son started to reside at House No. 369, situated at second floor, 6th cross, Hulimavu.
Thereafter, the said accused has continued to harass the deceased physically and mentally by abusing in filthy language and also assaulting to bring dowry of Rs.30,000/- from her mother.
Sometime the accused has sent the deceased along with their son to bring the amount.
As such, the deceased also started to work in garment, since the accused is being driver not going for work.
As the accused did not stop physical and mental torture towards the deceased and her son, hence the deceased fed up with the accused and decided to commit suicide.

Accordingly, on 06.06.2018 at 06.00 p.m. the deceased Malini has committed suicide by hanging herself at her matrimonial house and thereby the accused has committed the alleged offences as alleged against him.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned Judicial Magistrate,
Bangalore.

The learned Magistrate, after taking cognizance of the offences against the accused,
committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Section 207 of CrPC by furnishing copy of the charge sheet to the accused.

After committal, the said case was numbered as SC No. 1952 /2018.
4.

The charge was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A,
304-B of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined twelve witnesses and got marked documents at EX.P1 to P16, MO.1 to MO.4.

On consent of the accused counsel, the prosecution has got marked the death memo,
Postmortem report and Arrest of accused at Exhibit P11 to P13 respectively.
As such, Learned PP has gave up the witnesses CW12, CW13, CW15 to CW17.
Infact the material witnesses of the prosecution have turned hostile.
As such the prosecution side evidence was closed.

2 6.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, this court has recorded the statement of accused as provided under Section 313 of CrPC.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not opted to lead defence evidence nor submitted anything to the court.
The accused has complied Section 437A of CrPC.

7. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
8.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 married the daughter of C.W.1 by name Smt.T.Malini on 7.10.2011 at S.M.Kalyana Mantapa, Yelachenahalli,
Bengaluru, and out of the wedlock accused and Smt.Malini blessed with a male child and at the time of marriage, accused on demand received dowry from the parents of deceased and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sec.3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being husband of deceased Smt.Malini and after the marriage, when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused at house bearing No.362, 2nd floor situated at 6th cross, Hulimavu village,
within the limits of Hulimavu P.S, Bengaluru, accused under the influence of alcohol subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry in terms of cash and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sec.4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?

3. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of deceased Smt.Malini, and after marriage, when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused at Huimavu within the limits of Peenya PS., Bengaluru, accused subjected the deceased to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry of in terms of cash by abusing and assaulting her and ousted her and her son from the matrimonial house and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sec.498A of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being husband of deceased Smt.Malini and after marriage when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused at Hulimavu Grama within the limits of Hulimavu PS., Bengaluru, accused subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry in terms of cash from her parntal house by abusing and assaulting, and unable to tolerate the torture of accused deceased Smt.Malini had committed suicide on 06.06.2018 at 6.00 p.m and such cruelty and harassment as did drive the said deceased Smt.Malini to commit suicide within 7 years of marriage by hanging herself at her matrimonial house and accused being her husband, subjected her to cruelty and harassment in connection with the demand for additional dowry and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 304B of IPC?

3 5.
What order?

9. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: In the Negative  Point No.5: As per final order  for the following:
R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 to 4: All these points are taken up together for discussions as they are related with each other and to avoid repetition.

The mother of the deceased by name Lakshmi Devi, the son of the Lakshmi Devi i.e. brother of the deceased Dinesh Kumar, the brother of the complainant Thirumalai Swamy and son of the deceased by name Master Charan Kumar have been examined by the prosecution as PW1, PW9, PW4 and PW5 respectively.

The evidence of these witnesses, PW1, PW4, PW5 and PW9, denotes that the deceased Malini and accused were married each other on 07.10.2011 at S.M. Kalyana Mantapa,
Yelechenahalli, Bangalore, as per the customs prevailed in their family.
The evidence of said witnesses also reveals that after marriage, the accused and deceased Malini started their marital life along with parents of the deceased in the same house.
Due to the marital relationship between the accused and the deceased, the witness PW 5 Master Charan Kumar was born.
Except the marriage and born of child, nothing has been deposed by the said witnesses.

The said witnesses never given evidence regarding giving of physical and mental torture to the deceased by abusing in the filthy words and assaulting her by the accused and due to such torture and continuous harassment by the accused for money, the deceased had committed suicide by hanging herself at her matrimonial house.
As such, the prosecution could be set witnesses at the hospital and cross-examined with the permission of the court.
Unfortunately, all the said witnesses not supported the story of the prosecution, even though the learned PP has suggested the main allegations present against the accused.
Assessed the evidence of the family members of the deceased including her son, Master Charanakumar not helpful for the prosecution to establish a guilt against the accused.
11. It is necessary to note that the relatives of the complainant PW 6 Mamatha, PW 7 Raghuraman and PW8 Pattabirama have been examined by the prosecution.
The witnesses PW6, PW7, being the signatories to the inquest mahazar marked at Exhibit P6, not supported the conducting of inquest mahazar as per Exhibit P6 on the dead body of the deceased Malini.

However, the witness PW7 has stated before the court about the conducting of inquest mahazar, but in the cross examination of the accused counsel, the said witness admitted he doesn't know the contents of the inquest mahazar.
It appears these witnesses PW6 to PW8 just signatories to the inquest mahazar marked at ExP6.

It Hulimavu Ps vs Naveen Kumar on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196027100/
4 means the police have just obtained the signature of the said witnesses as a procedure.

sentences.text: If not, the said witnesses would have clearly deposed about the conducting of the said mahazar, if at all, it was carried out in the presence of the said witnesses.
So also, the witness PW8 Pattabirama has denied the giving of physical and mental harassment to the deceased by the accused demanding the cash.
So the evidence of the said witness goes against to the statement recorded by the Thasildar at the time of conducting the inquest mahazar.
As such the learned PP treated the said witness as hostile and cross examined, but unable to get any worthful evidence in support of the prosecution story.
It is very clear that the evidence given by these witnesses PW6 to 8 also not at all support the prosecution story in any angle to prove the guilt against the accused.
12. The prosecution succeeded to examine the owner of the house by name Sunil as P.W.2 and the neighbour of the house Mr.Jayaprakash as P.W.3.
It is an admitted fact that the deceased and accused were tenant under the witness P.W.2 Mr.Sunil.

But the said witness being the signatory to the spot Mahazar and given statement before the police about the alleged incident, but the said witness evidence shows that he is not aware about the contents of spot Mahazar marked at Ex.P.4 and so also he has not supported the prosecution by deposing that there was no quarrel between the accused and deceased at any time and they were leading good and happy married life.

So also, the neighbour witness P.W.3 Jayapakash failed to support the prosecution case by deposing he do not know how the deceased and accused leading their life and he never seen the quarrel between the accused and deceased about relating to the bringing of dowry by the deceased.
As such, the learned Public Prosecutor though cross-examined these 2 witnesses PWs.2 and 3 treated them as hostile the permission of court to enable to get any useful evidence.
So, the evidence given by these witnesses also not helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
13. The another witness P.W.10 Sarathi, being the signatory to spot Mahazar Ex.P.4 also did not supported the conducting of spot Mahazar by saying that he do not know its contents.
So, it appears the Investigation Officer has not carried out the spot Mahazar in the presence of this witness.

Even in the cross-examination, the learned Public Prosecutor failed to get any evidence to prove the conducting of spot by the Investigation Officer at spot in the presence of this witness and P.W.2 Mr.Sunil.
So, the evidence given by all the independent witnesses not at all helpful to the prosecution in any angle.
14. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.12 Chadananda Navi has registered the FIR as per Ex.P.15 by receiving the complaint as per Ex.P.1 on 07.06.2018 at 7.30 p.m.

On 08.06.2018 he has submitted requisition as per Ex.P.16 to C.W.14 to conduct inquest Mahazar on the dead body of the deceased and thereafter handed over further investigation to P.W.11/C.W.19 Mr.Ramesh.K.N the then ACP.
The said witness P.W.11 after receiving further investigation has visited the spot on 08.06.2018 and conducted spot Mahazar in the presence of panchas as per Ex.P.4.
Thereafter on the same day, he has collected the clothes of the deceased Malini handed over by the medical Officer at the time of conducting post mortem.
The said clothes brought into the PF and submitted to the court.
The said clothes were brought by C.W.17 and handed over to P.W.11 and submitted report as per Ex.P.14.
The said witness identified the clothes marked at M.Os.1 to 4.
He has also given instructions to CWs.16 and 18 to trace and produce the accused before him and accordingly issued Memo.

On 09.06.2018 he has recorded statement of CWs.2 to 7 and on the same day, the witness Hulimavu Ps vs Naveen Kumar on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196027100/
5

sentences.text: Chidananda Navi produced the accused before him.
Immediately he has carried out arrest procedure and after medical examination produced the accused alongwith remand application and police escort before the court for judicial custody.
Thereafter he has recorded statement of C.W.16.
On the same day, he has collected the marriage invitation and photos as per Ex.P.2 and 3 related to the deceased and accused produced by C.W.4 i.e. brother of the deceased.
On 23.06.2018, collected P.M.Report as per Ex.P.12 related to the deceased from Victoria hospital.
Since the investigation was completed and as there is evidence against the accused, hence submitted charge sheet against the accused before the court.
15. The evidence of both police official witnesses PWs.11 and 12 completely denied by accused counsel.
The evidence given by the independent witnesses and these official witnesses not match with each other.

So, there is no corroborative evidence between the witnesses and also the evidence given by the witnesses completely contrary to the documents prepared by the Investigation Officer during the investigation.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has completely failed to establish the guilt against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 4 in the Negative.

16. Point No.5: In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 4, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
M.Os.1 to 4 clothes are being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after expiry of appeal time.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 08 th day of October, 2025)
(E. RAJEEVA GOWDA) XLV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru
